name: CausalFunnel A/B Testing
author: causalfunnel

sections.description:
CausalFunnel A/B Testing helps site owners create, launch, and evaluate conversion experiments from the WordPress dashboard.

Features include:

  • Page, post, URL, headline, button, element, and WooCommerce product tests.
  • Audience targeting by device, browser, country, referrer, UTM parameters, and time.
  • Conversion goals and experiment result reporting.
  • Optional analytics, heatmap, and customer-journey integrations.
  • Optional AI-assisted test suggestions.

Analytics Dashboard and Website Tracking are enabled by default so experiments work immediately. Site owners can disable either feature in CF Platform → Account Info after reviewing the details below.

External services

This plugin connects to CausalFunnel services when the relevant feature is enabled. All external requests are consent-gated.

  • apps.causalfunnels.com — experiment configuration, conversion metrics, and optional Google Analytics/Tag Manager integration. Sends test configuration, variant assignments, page URLs, pseudonymous session/device identifiers, event type, device type, and optional conversion value.
  • server.causalfunnels.com — analytics, heatmaps, customer-journey reports, geolocation, and page audits. Sends site identifier, page URL, date range, or visitor IP (for geolocation). Requests occur when an administrator opens a report or starts an audit.
  • agent.causalfunnels.com — AI-powered test suggestions and audits. Sends product names, prices, descriptions, categories, stock status, site identifier, and business context. Requires analytics consent and occurs only when an administrator starts the AI feature.
  • www.scripts.causalfunnel.com — serves the consent-gated frontend A/B-testing script.

Admin JavaScript and CSS dependencies are bundled locally.

Review the CausalFunnel privacy policy before enabling external integrations. Site owners are responsible for obtaining any consent required by their jurisdiction. For data deletion requests, contact CausalFunnel support.

Privacy and cookies

The following cookies are created only after consent is enabled:

  • cf_prevDeviceId and cf_prevBrowserId (up to 365 days): Pseudonymous browser/device identifiers.
  • cf_visitor_id (up to 365 days): Session identifier for tracking.
  • cf_prod_test_* (up to 30 days): A/B test variant assignments for returning visitors.
  • cf_view_* (up to 1 hour): Prevents duplicate pageview recording on reload.

Disable data collection in Account Info to stop new tracking and cookie creation. Previously issued cookies expire naturally or can be cleared by the site owner. Existing data stored by CausalFunnel services is governed by the service’s retention and deletion policies.

Support

For support and service documentation, visit CausalFunnel.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the causalfunnel-datascience folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the ZIP from the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open CF Platform → Account Info.
  4. Review the privacy and external-service information.
  5. Disable any feature your site does not require.
  6. Create and launch an A/B test from CF Platform → A/B Tests.

WooCommerce product tests require WooCommerce. Elementor deployment features require Elementor.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin work without WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce is only required for product A/B tests. All other test types work independently.

Can I disable data collection?

Yes. Analytics Dashboard and Website Tracking can be disabled at any time in CF Platform → Account Info.

Is this plugin compatible with caching plugins?

Yes. The A/B testing script uses client-side variant assignment, so it works with page-level caching.

How do I delete data collected by CausalFunnel?

Contact CausalFunnel support for remote data deletion requests. Disable data collection in Account Info to stop new data from being sent.
sections.changelog:
2.3.4

  • Ensured Analytics Dashboard and Website Tracking default to enabled when their options are missing.
  • Added a versioned upgrade migration that enables both permissions for existing installations.

2.3.3

  • Enabled Analytics Dashboard and Website Tracking by default for new installations and existing installations during a one-time migration.
  • Added the onboarding spotlight tour for the plugin workspace and reporting tools.

2.3.2

  • Security: added nonce verification to all AJAX handlers.
  • Privacy: consent checks enforced on all external API calls.
  • Localised admin JavaScript and CSS dependencies.
  • Updated text domain to causalfunnel for consistency.
  • Compatibility: tested up to WordPress 7.1.

2.3

  • Version bump with updated readme disclosures and gitignore.
